title: Regional evacuation coordinator: staged readiness transitions and probe escort to stabilize autoscaling
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: During recent multi-region degradations we observed correlated probe failures triggering large-scale readiness flips and autoscaler thrash. Symptoms: mass pod evictions, aggressive scale-downs, and long warmup tails that breached customer latency SLOs. Goal: implement a regional evacuation coordinator that gracefully converts capacity through staged readiness transitions (soft-ready -> guarded-ready -> fully-ready), escorts health-probe traffic to reduce fanout, and stabilizes autoscaler decisions during region failover and recovery.

Scope and out-of-band constraints:
- This is a serving-runtime and control-plane coordinated change. The control-plane will orchestrate state transitions; node agents will implement local readiness state machine.
- Backwards compatibility: new readiness states must be ignored by older control-plane versions (default to current k8s semantics).
- Must not block dedicated private deployments (feature flagged).

High level design:
1) Staged readiness transitions: introduce two intermediate readiness states (GUARDED and WARMING). Services transition: NotReady -> WARMING (allow synthetic warmups & low-priority traffic) -> GUARDED (full non-critical traffic, limited QPS) -> Ready. Transitions driven by coordinator policies and metrics.
2) Probe escort and sampling: reduce probe fanout in failover by sampling readiness probes at a regional quorum. Probe traffic will be routed through a lightweight "escort" proxy that caches recent responses and answers probes for short windows, preventing stampedes.
3) Autoscaler stabilization: tie HPA/vertical decisions to an aggregated health envelope with hysteresis. Autoscaler will ignore transient health dips under a configured grace window and rely on synthetic sentinel checks to confirm real capacity loss.
4) Circuit quarantine: when a region is flapping, mark routes as quarantined and apply stepped capacity handoff with token-weighted request routing to avoid sudden load shifts.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong consistency vs availability for readiness state: chosen eventual consistency with short lease windows to avoid global blockers.
- Probe caching increases time-to-detect certain failures (e.g., complete node loss); we mitigate with synthetic checks and escalations.
- Additional control-plane complexity vs on-node simplicity: offloaded orchestration to control-plane to keep node agents minimal and easier to roll out.

Planned tasks (breaking into PR-sized pieces):
- TC1: Coordinator API and CRD (control-plane): record region lifecycle and per-service readiness policy (ENG-531999-1).
- TC2: Node agent readiness state machine and local cache (ENG-531999-2).
- TC3: Probe escort proxy implementation and integration tests (ENG-531999-3).
- TC4: Autoscaler adapter: aggregate health envelope and hysteresis policy (ENG-531999-4).
- TC5: Synthetic sentinel harness and dashboards (ENG-531999-5).
- TC6: Canary rollout plan + chaos exercise to validate (ENG-531999-6).

Acceptance criteria:
- On simulated regional outage, average pod eviction rate reduced by >= 70% compared to baseline (dashboard: Grafana link).
- End-to-end failover completes without SLO breach for 95th percentile latency for critical routes in 3/3 canaries.
- Autoscaler thrash metric (scale events per 10m) reduced by >= 60% during failover/recovery windows.
- All new APIs covered by unit/integration tests and documented in Confluence PRD.

Links and artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Regional+Evacuation+Coordinator+PRD
- Incident deck (postmortem): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-evacuation-postmortem
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/evac-coordinator/evacuation-metrics
- Initial spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8345

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag gated in control-plane. Start with internal-only region on a low-traffic cluster.
- Progressive canary: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% by region with observability gates at each step.
- Chaos tests: region blackhole and network partition scenarios executed before wider rollout.

Open questions / risks:
- How to tune sample rates for probe escort to avoid masking real long-tail failures? (Action: simulation harness to sweep sample rates.)
- Interaction with third-party ingress controllers and customers' custom readiness checks. (Action: compatibility tests and a migration guide.)
- Potential billing/chargeback implications for Dedicated customers during staged traffic shifts. (Action: finance review during Cycle 10.)

- Create feature-flag and CRD scaffolding (owner: Asha; ETA 2026-03-08).

technical_notes: Probe escort will run as a sidecar-less, ephemeral proxy implemented in Rust for low-latency path; uses in-memory LRU cache with TTL derived from probe type.
Coordinator will expose a lightweight gRPC API; backward-compatible behavior: unknown readiness states treated as NotReady by older control planes.
Autoscaler adapter will compute health_envelope = weighted_percentile(ready_ratio, latency_p95, synthetic_pass_rate) with tunable hysteresis windows.
Chaos harness scripts added: scripts/evac_simulate.sh (simulate network partitions and rapid region recovery).
acceptance_criteria: <= 30% of baseline pod evictions during multi-region failover in canary runs
No SLO breach (p95) for critical routes across 3 consecutive canary windows
Observed autoscaler scale event rate reduced by >= 60% during fail/recover tests
Feature flag present and toggleable per-organization for Dedicated/private deployments
